input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Frequency is expressly capped: § 22.1 (p0082) permits Vendor to audit "no more than once in any twelve-month period," which is the preferred once-per-12-months limit; any automated 'audit frequency limited: false' signal is a false negative against that operative language. The same paragraph supplies the remaining preferred conduct terms — at least thirty days' prior written notice, normal business hours, no unreasonable disruption, off-site where practicable, and an independent auditor bound by confidentiality. § 22.2 (p0083) puts audit costs on Vendor unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent, and expressly bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information, satisfying the cost-allocation and no-system-access elements and avoiding the walk-away position. § 22.3 (p0084) adds protection by making findings Customer Confidential Information usable only to enforce the Agreement. No broader inspection, verification, monitoring or remote-access right binds Customer elsewhere: Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) contains only a heading with no operative text, and a document-wide search for inspection, monitoring, premises and telemetry rights returned nothing running against Customer. The clause meets the preferred position, so no redline or counterparty comment is required.
